summary: Translation exercise (28 sentences) on expressing possession with minulla on / minulla ei ole + partitive, family members, nationalities and being hungry/thirsty/hot/cold.
transcript:
TO HAVE: MINULLA ON ISOSISKO, MUTTA MINULLA EI OLE ISOVELJEÄ
I have a big (older) sister, but I don’t have a big (older) brother
Kuinka sanot suomeksi:
1. I have a little sister. (little sister= pikkusisko)
2. Do you have a little sister?
3. She has a big brother.
4. My father has a big brother.
5. But he doesn’t have a big sister.
6. You have a young Mother. (young= nuori)
7. How old is your Father?
8. They have a lovely stepmother. (lovely= ihana, stepmother= äitipuoli)
9. Their daughter is 5 years old.
10. They have one daughter and one son.
11. I don’t have a grandmother. She is deceased. (deceased= kuollut)
12. My parents are retired. (parents= vanhemmat)
13. They don’t have a good pension. (pension= eläke)
14. Do they have an apartment of their own? (we say: ”own apartment”= oma asunto TAI omistusasunto)
15. Susanna has a sister but she doesn’t have a brother.
16. I don’t have an apartment of my own. But my boyfriend has his own apartment.
17. I am hungry.
18. Are you (plural ”you”) thirsty?
19. We are hot. Are you hot?
20. Is he cold? - Yes. He doesn’t have a thick coat with him. (thick= paksu, coat= takki, with him= mukana)
21. Do they have an French Mother?
22. No, they don’t. But my sister has a new husband. He is French. (new= uusi)
23. Does her husband have any children? (any children= lapsia)
24. They have a German father and an Estonian mother.
25. My father is English and my mother is Scottish.
26. Is your brother married? - Yes. He has a Russian wife.
27. Do they have any children?
27. No, they don’t. But they have a dog. The dog’s name is Panu and their dog has its own bed. (bed= peti)

title.fi: Minulla on isosisko, mutta minulla ei ole isoveljeä
title.en: I have a big sister, but I don't have a big brother

lines.fi: Minulla on isosisko, mutta minulla ei ole isoveljeä.
lines.en: I have a big (older) sister, but I don't have a big (older) brother.

exercises.title: Kuinka sanot suomeksi
exercises.instruction: How do you say in Finnish (to have: minulla on / minulla ei ole + partitive).

items.prompt: I have a little sister.
Do you have a little sister?
She has a big brother.
My father has a big brother.
But he doesn't have a big sister.
You have a young Mother.
How old is your Father?
They have a lovely stepmother.
Their daughter is 5 years old.
items.answer: Heidän tyttärensä on viisi vuotta vanha.

items.prompt: They have one daughter and one son.
items.answer: Heillä on yksi tytär ja yksi poika.

items.prompt: I don't have a grandmother. She is deceased.
items.answer: Minulla ei ole isoäitiä. Hän on kuollut.

items.prompt: My parents are retired.
They don't have a good pension.
Do they have an apartment of their own?
Susanna has a sister but she doesn't have a brother.
items.answer: Susannalla on sisko, mutta hänellä ei ole veljeä.

items.prompt: I don't have an apartment of my own. But my boyfriend has his own apartment.
items.answer: Minulla ei ole omaa asuntoa. Mutta minun poikaystävälläni on oma asunto.

items.prompt: I am hungry.
Are you (plural "you") thirsty?
We are hot. Are you hot?
items.answer: Meillä on kuuma. Onko sinulla kuuma?

items.prompt: Is he cold? - Yes. He doesn't have a thick coat with him.
items.answer: Onko hänellä kylmä? – Kyllä. Hänellä ei ole paksua takkia mukana.

items.prompt: Do they have an French Mother?
No, they don't. But my sister has a new husband. He is French.
items.answer: Ei ole. Mutta minun siskollani on uusi mies. Hän on ranskalainen.

items.prompt: Does her husband have any children?
They have a German father and an Estonian mother.
items.answer: Heillä on saksalainen isä ja virolainen äiti.

items.prompt: My father is English and my mother is Scottish.
items.answer: Minun isäni on englantilainen ja minun äitini on skotlantilainen.

items.prompt: Is your brother married? - Yes. He has a Russian wife.
items.answer: Onko sinun veljesi naimisissa? – Kyllä. Hänellä on venäläinen vaimo.

items.prompt: Do they have any children?
No, they don't. But they have a dog. The dog's name is Panu and their dog has its own bed.
items.answer: Ei ole. Mutta heillä on koira. Koiran nimi on Panu ja heidän koirallaan on oma peti.

grammar_notes.heading: TO HAVE
grammar_notes.text: Possession = owner in the adessive (-lla/-llä) + on: minulla on isosisko. Negative: minulla ei ole + partitive (isoveljeä). Feelings: minulla on nälkä / jano / kuuma / kylmä.
